Family.title: Family
Family.description: Represents a family group within the application.

owner.description: The UID of the user who owns/created the family.

memberIds.description: References to UserProfiles who are members of this family. (Relationship: Family 1:N UserProfile)

id.description: Unique identifier for the user profile.

familyId.description: Reference to the Family this user belongs to. (Relationship: Family 1:N UserProfile)

Photo.title: Photo
Photo.description: Represents a photo uploaded by a user.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who uploaded the photo. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Photo)

familyId.description: Reference to the Family the photo belongs to. (Relationship: Family 1:N Photo)

storageUrl.description: URL of the photo stored in Cloud Storage.

textNote.description: Optional text note associated with the photo.

voiceNoteUrl.description: Optional URL of a voice note associated with the photo.

tagIds.description: References to Tags associated with the photo. (Relationship: Photo N:N Tag)

uploadDate.description: Date and time when the photo was uploaded.

Tag.title: Tag
Tag.description: Represents a tag that can be associated with photos.

photoIds.description: References to Photos associated with the tag. (Relationship: Photo N:N Tag)

SpecialDay.title: SpecialDay
SpecialDay.description: Represents a special day or milestone (birthday, anniversary).

id.description: Unique identifier for the special day.

familyId.description: Reference to the Family the special day belongs to. (Relationship: Family 1:N SpecialDay)

type.description: Type of special day (e.g., birthday, anniversary).

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to ensure Authorization Independence, support QAPs, and maintain data integrity. User profiles and families are stored in top-level collections (`userProfiles` and `families` respectively). Photos are stored in a subcollection under families (`/families/{familyId}/photos/{photoId}`) which simplifies security rules based on family membership. Each `Photo` document includes denormalized `familyId` and `userId`, allowing security rules to validate that the user uploading the photo is indeed a member of the family. SpecialDays are also stored under families (`/families/{familyId}/specialDays/{specialDayId}`) to ensure easy management and querying within the context of a family.  Tags are stored in a top-level collection and are related to Photos via the `tagIds` array stored on the Photo entity. This design achieves Authorization Independence by including all necessary authorization data within the Photo document, avoiding the need for `get()` calls in security rules. QAPs are supported through structural segregation; listing photos under a family inherently filters results to only those accessible to family members.
